declared_cadence: event-driven (as-required) — updates only while Parliament sits

known_quirks: The Hansard catalogue (sittings, MPs, parliamentary terms) is event-driven: it advances only when Parliament sits and publishes new records.

The official 15th Parliament 2026 Fifth Session sitting calendar runs 19 Jan–3 Mar, 22 Jun–4 Aug (Dewan Negara), and 5 Oct–8 Dec 2026; a no-sitting recess between meetings is a normal gap, not a feed failure.
content_freshness_date reflects the latest sitting (or term end), not a daily or weekly publication timestamp.

known_false_positives.description: A normal intra-sessional parliamentary recess (e.g. 4 Aug to 5 Oct 2026, ~60 days) leaves content_freshness_date unchanged, so a weekly cadence wrongly flags the row stale. Hansard is event-driven (as-required) and must not be reported stale across a sitting-calendar recess.
known_false_positives.detection_signal: refresh_frequency=as-required AND content_freshness_date within the official sitting-calendar recess window

known_false_negatives: A genuinely halted Hansard export (content_freshness_date older than the conservative 270-day null-cadence stale boundary) still classifies stale under the as-required null-cadence default.

failure_examples.cause: Weekly cadence applied to an event-driven source during the 4 Aug–5 Oct recess.
failure_examples.resolution: Declare refresh_frequency=as-required so a recess gap classifies fresh.

current_probe_rule: scripts/check.sh dispatches the hansard-script adapter (extract_hansard_probe_metrics) which reads the latest sitting/term/MP date as content_freshness_date; staleness falls to the conservative 90-day null-cadence default for as-required rows.
re_audit_trigger: Parliament of Malaysia Third Meeting starts 5 Oct 2026; re-audit Hansard cadence after the first sitting to confirm the event-driven declaration.
